report.summary: Analyzed chunk 1 of 3 of daedalus/wiki/links.py: defines WikiLink dataclass, extract_wikilinks, LinkIndex, constants, and regex for wikilinks. Verified claims about link forms, refusal to guess, bounded limits, and local graph philosophy.

handoff.purpose: Define wikilink parsing, data structures, and local graph philosophy for the wiki link system.

symbols.name: LINKS_VERSION
symbols.note: Version string '1' for the link index.

symbols.name: MAX_LINKS_PER_PAGE
symbols.note: Maximum number of links extracted per page, set to 500.

symbols.name: MAX_MENTIONS_PER_PAGE
symbols.note: Maximum number of mentions per page, set to 50.

symbols.name: MAX_LOCAL_NODES
symbols.note: Maximum number of nodes in local graph, set to 200.

symbols.name: _WIKILINK
symbols.note: Regex pattern to match wikilinks including embed, target, anchor, and alias.

symbols.name: WikiLink
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass representing a parsed wikilink with kind, target, anchor, alias, embed, line.

symbols.name: WikiLink.to_dict
symbols.note: Returns dict representation of the WikiLink.

symbols.name: extract_wikilinks
symbols.note: Extracts all wikilinks from a page body string, returning list of WikiLink objects. No I/O.

symbols.name: LinkIndex
symbols.note: Dataclass holding forward/backward link maps, code_links, type_links, cross_vault, unresolved lists.

claims.text: the local walk is the primary product here and the global one is not built at all
claims.why: No global graph construction is present in this chunk.

claims.text: ``[[Note]]``                 a page, by title or by path
claims.why: The regex _WIKILINK matches [[target]] and extract_wikilinks sets kind to DOC for targets without prefix.
Regex captures optional #anchor group, and WikiLink stores anchor.

claims.text: ``[[Note|shown text]]``      an alias; the target is unchanged
claims.why: Regex captures optional |alias group, and WikiLink stores alias.

claims.text: ``![[Note]]``                an embed rather than a link — a different relation
claims.why: Regex captures optional !embed group, and WikiLink stores embed boolean.

claims.text: ``[[code:path/to/f.py]]``    a doc -> code edge (Swimm's idea: a real edge, not a URL)
claims.why: extract_wikilinks checks for 'code:' prefix and sets kind to CODE.
Regex captures anchor after #, and extract_wikilinks sets kind to CODE for 'code:' prefix.

claims.text: ``[[type:TypeName]]``        a doc -> type edge; PARSED and COUNTED, never resolved here, because the type layer is built separately and importing it would couple the wiki to an index build
claims.why: extract_wikilinks sets kind to TYPE for 'type:' prefix; no resolution code present.

claims.text: ``[[vault:name/page]]``      cross-vault. Parsed so it is visible, resolved only when a registry is supplied — and DEFERRED as a feature, because cross-vault resolution needs the multi-root join nobody has built.
claims.why: extract_wikilinks sets kind to VAULT for 'vault:' prefix; no resolution code present.

claims.text: a link that does not resolve to something present is DROPPED and COUNTED, never bound to a near-match; a link matching MORE THAN ONE candidate is AMBIGUOUS and produces no edge at all.
claims.why: Resolution logic is not in this chunk; only parsing is present.

claims.text: Every wikilink in a page body, in source order. No resolution, no I/O.
claims.why: Function uses regex finditer which returns matches in order; no I/O or resolution performed.

claims.text: Forward and reverse edges over one vault. Derived; regenerate and it is true.
claims.why: No methods for derivation or regeneration are present in this chunk.

observations.what: extract_wikilinks uses a binary search on line starts for line number calculation, which is efficient but assumes starts list is sorted.
The prefix matching for kind is case-insensitive (raw.lower().startswith(prefix)), but the regex target group may contain mixed case; this is consistent with typical wiki behavior.
LinkIndex fields are typed as dict and list but not constrained; forward and backward are defaultdict(list) via lambda, but type hints use plain dict.
The regex _WIKILINK allows empty anchor or alias; these are stored as empty strings and later stripped.
The chunk does not include any code for resolving links, building the index, or handling cross-vault links; those are deferred.
